convoLines.text: "I keep dreaming about rows of pods. Humming. Tell me I'm not the only one."
You can feel the history in how they greet you.

"It's my aunt, Emily. Went in the Taking. She laughed like a screen door in a windstorm. Boring. Right. Some nights I swear I hear them before I sleep -- the pods, rows deep, humming. Then morning comes and I can't say whether it was real."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"I dreamed Felipe was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
"Out there? With YOU leading? ...Let me think about it."
"I keep turning over the last thing Felipe said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"Still on what's been happening."
You show them Stinging Nettle — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Thanks for listening. Most people change the subject."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Have you ever hurt someone? Since all this started."
They nod, slow. "Okay. Thank you for telling me. That couldn't have been easy to say."
"I don't keep score on that. Score-keeping is how you stop sleeping. I do what the day needs and I don't rehearse it after."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Still on whether you've hurt someone."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Never mind the pantry run — we got it handled. Thanks anyway. I can't reach this properly. Will you help me clean it?"
"It's getting worse, not better. If it festers I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. Just clean it out and wrap it tight."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Felipe is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
"Sleep's gone strange. I memorize the stars at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"Alright. Catch you later."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"We never finished talking about what's been happening — we got cut off, 4 days back. 'A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.'"
"Come see what I found. You won't believe it."
Halfway to the hollow, Moshe freezes. Fresh tracks — big. "We go back now. Quietly." You do. The wild, reminding you.
"The fire feels smaller without Felipe. The rest of us will have to be bigger."
"I'm picking up Felipe's share of the work. Someone should, and it might as well be me."
"Still on what's been happening. That's still where we are."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good — what's been happening, settled. Feels better said out loud."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Never mind this wound — we got it handled. Thanks anyway."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Good question." "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "Since Felipe died... I keep expecting to see Felipe at the fire. Stupid."
Their friendliness thins — still there, just held at arm's length.
"I memorize the stars for Felipe, now. Feels right. Feels like the least I can do."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Ethan grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Ethan is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on what's been happening."
You show them Stinging Nettle — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Right. Go on, then."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Never mind the food I needed — we got it handled. Thanks anyway."
They light up a little when they see you.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"

"Huh. Let me think about that." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "You want to know what I did in the raid? I met The Redactor at the treeline and barely walked away. Don't call it brave. Call it awake."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Ethan nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"I wish there was more to tell. That's it."
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Like I said — Still on what's been happening."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.

"We never finished talking about what's been happening — we got cut off, 7 days back. 'You show them Stinging Nettle — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. And I've been walking…' We still owe that sickness help a proper ending, too."
"That's... pretty much all of it, honestly."
"Yeah? What's up?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "I'd follow you out past the treeline. Don't tell the others — they'd want to come too."
"Here's what it would take, if you want more than this: show up when it costs you something. That's the whole test."
"Still on each other."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"I should get back to it."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Ha. You again. I don't mind this."
"Walk my trap line with me? Extra hands, extra eyes."
It's quiet at the trap line. Moshe doesn't say much. Sometimes that's the whole point.

"Huh. Let me think about that." "Last time things were different. They always are." "When I was bleeding, Eduardo stayed and did the work. That's what I keep coming back to."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."

"...Think about it? I'll be around."

Ethan: "Hey — come here. You should hear this."
Their whole posture softens around you.
"We're eating through stores faster than we replace them. Forage with me tomorrow? I know the creek bend, past the treeline."
"The stores won't stretch past tomorrow, and I'm not choosing who eats. I know the creek bend, past the treeline — come with me and we'll fill packs before dark."
Your partner is inside the Haven hall. Go through the door to meet them.

"You want to know about that? Okay." "Don't laugh. Never seeing home again."

"Mumbles the plan out loud — that's what I do when the fear gets loud. You've probably noticed."
"Still on what scares them."

Ethan shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
"Twelve strangers. One of them has to be my person. Statistics demand it."

deathBeat: d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Felipe Rinaldi is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d41: 🕯️ Felipe Rinaldi is dead — a hushwolf. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d41: The village's quarrel was with Felipe — and Felipe is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d42: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. The Loud Beast is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
recoverHome: d42: That night, they bring Felipe home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
vouch: d41: At the grave, Moshe, Ethan, Jesse speak for Eduardo — "Felipe trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
burialWindowSay: d41: The village's quarrel was with Felipe — and Felipe is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.

d44: You say a few words for Felipe. Not a ceremony — just: you were here, and someone noticed you leaving. (-3 trauma)
d44: You bury Felipe. A marker, of sorts. The village will know where. (+4 trauma)
echoSample: d44: "I dreamed Felipe was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
d44: "I keep turning over the last thing Felipe said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
d44: "Felipe is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
d48: "The fire feels smaller without Felipe. The rest of us will have to be bigger."
d48: "I'm picking up Felipe's share of the work. Someone should, and it might as well be me."
d48: "Good question." "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "Since Felipe died... I keep expecting to see Felipe at the fire. Stupid."
echoV2Sample: d44: The village raises a marker by the fire — Felipe, day 44. a hushwolf. A place to stand.
echoV2DeltaSample: d44: The village raises a marker by the fire — Felipe, day 44. a hushwolf. A place to stand.
halfRationLines: d70: "The bins are echoing. We vote half rations — three days, everyone, no exceptions — or the hunters go out hungry and bring back more than hunger."
